The mechanic

One page.
Two businesses.

This company builds in daylight and lights at night — so the site does too. Same page, same content, lit by the same clock the crews work to. Drag the rail and watch which half of the business steps forward.

06:00 — 18:45 · Daylight

Build it

In daylight the site sells construction. Commercial buildouts, tenant improvements, demolition through finishes, electrical rough-in, panels and permits. The buyer is a tenant with a lease clock running.

  • E-Built
  • Buildouts
  • Electrical
  • Remodelling
  • Property services
18:45 — 06:00 · After dark

Light it

After dark the site sells lighting. Landscape and permanent systems, architectural facades, parking lots, the work that only exists once the sun is down. The buyer is looking at a dark property and wants it to look like this one.

  • E-Lighting
  • Landscape
  • Permanent
  • Parking lot
  • Maintenance
Why this is the concept

The audience split was the hardest problem in the strategy — commercial buyers read proof and schedules, residential buyers read photographs. Every solution costs something. Here the clock does the work for free, and the visitor never sees a compromise. It is also, as far as I can find, not something any lighting or electrical contractor has done.

The shoot, precisely

The renderings above stand in for the real thing. What replaces them: five or six finished jobs, a phone, a cheap tripod, and a piece of tape on the ground so the second visit lands in the same spot. One frame at 2pm, the same frame at 9pm. Nothing else. Without matched pairs there is no Dusk — and with real ones, this grid becomes the most persuasive thing on the site.

Signature interaction

The decision
everyone gets wrong

Colour temperature is the choice customers regret most, and nobody explains it. So let them feel it — this is the same room, the same fixtures, the same wattage. Only the Kelvin changes.

2700K Warm White

Restaurants, hotels, landscape, residential. Warm light flatters skin, wood and stone, and it reads as hospitality. This is what almost every home exterior should be — and what most contractors get wrong by installing something colder and cheaper.

Why a jury notices this

It is a tool, not a brochure. It teaches something true in about four seconds, it is drawn from the client's actual expertise, and it makes the palette itself interactive. The same control quietly qualifies the visitor — someone who drags to 5000K is shopping for a warehouse, not a patio.

Concept prototype

What this is,
and isn't

Read before showing the client

The hero and the grid are AI-generated conceptual renderings, made as matched day/night pairs so each night frame holds the same camera position as its daylight partner. They are labelled as renderings wherever they appear, and they are not photographs of this company's work — nothing on this page was built by anyone. The colour-temperature room below is still drawn in code.

They exist to prove the mechanic with convincing imagery. What real photography changes: these become real Miami jobs, and the site stops being a demo and becomes theirs. The mechanic is finished. The real pictures are the gap.
